title: Channel faders at or below unity
rationale: Faders pushed above unity erode master headroom.
remediation: Gain-stage below 0 dB; raise the source gain instead if needed.

title: Return tracks exist for shared effects
rationale: Shared reverb/delay on returns is cleaner and lighter than per-channel inserts.
remediation: Add a return track and send channels to it for time-based effects.

title: Reverb/delay balance serves the mix
rationale: Wet/dry balance and depth are judgment calls best heard, not measured.

title: Tracks don't fight in the same frequency band
rationale: Two sources with near-identical spectral profiles mask each other, muddying the mix; high pairwise band overlap flags candidates for EQ carving or arrangement separation.
remediation: EQ-carve complementary space, pan apart, or thin the arrangement so the overlapping tracks don't compete.

title: No track buried far below the loudest
rationale: A track sitting more than ~12 LU below the loudest active track is likely lost in the mix; large integrated-loudness spread suggests a balance problem.
remediation: Raise the buried track's level (or duck competitors) until it reads in the mix; re-check after.

title: Per-track peaks leave headroom and aren't over-squashed
rationale: A track peaking above -1 dBTP eats master headroom and risks inter-sample clipping; a crest factor below ~4 dB signals over-compression that flattens dynamics.
remediation: Trim track gain to leave headroom; back off compression/limiting where crest is too low.

title: Stereo content stays mono-compatible
rationale: Strongly negative inter-channel correlation cancels on mono fold-down, so a widened track can vanish on mono playback (clubs, phones, Bluetooth).
remediation: Narrow the offending track's stereo image or check it in mono; keep low-frequency content centered.
